title: Fallback Variant Canvas: Console validator + simulated preview for region/tier routing
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Add a Canvas-style editor and a validation/preview surface in Console that lets customers author region selection + tier routing policies with explicit fallback model variants. The feature provides: (1) drag/drop rule blocks for region + tier conditions, (2) prioritized fallback lists of compatible model variants, (3) simulated traffic preview with latency/cost estimation, and (4) an automated safety linter with explainable fixes recommended to the user.
acceptance_criteria: Canvas editor available under Console > Routing > New Policy and supports creating rules with condition nodes: region, tier, customer_tier_label, model_family
Users can attach an ordered fallback chain of model variants to any route and mark compatibility constraints (e.g., quantized-only, >8k context).

Preview runner simulates a configurable traffic mix (region weights, request qps, median seq length) and produces per-route estimations: expected latency P50/P95, token cost delta, and estimated failover frequency.
Validation linter surfaces high-risk configurations (e.g., no fallback for critical regions, circular fallbacks, incompatible variant pairing) and provides suggested fixes with one-click apply.
Changes save as versioned policies and can be toggled into a dry-run preview or promoted to active rollout with canary percentage settings.
steps: Prototype Canvas flow with mocked rule blocks (UX spike) — Design
Define policy JSON schema extension to include fallbackVariantList and compatibilityConstraints — Eng (runtime + API)
Build preview simulator engine that reuses existing latency/cost profiling dataset in infra/telemetry — Eng (infra)
Implement linter rules and explainable fix engine (mapping lint -> PRD action) — Eng + PM
Integrate save/version and rollout toggles with Console backend endpoints — Eng (console + api)
User testing and iterate on recommended fixes and messaging — PM + Design
decisions: Keep policy authoring in Console (no separate studio app) to reduce cognitive context switching for admins.
Preview uses a deterministic simulator that samples from historical workload histograms rather than live traffic replay to avoid customer data leakage.
Fallback lists are ordered and resolved by the runtime using first-match; Console will show clear indicators when a fallback variant is in a different region/tier and may incur cross-region latency.
Model compatibility checks are conservative: if metadata is missing, show a warning and default to blocking activation until resolved.
Initially support three kinds of constraints: context-window, quantization-capability, and model-size class. Additional constraints may be added in later iterations.
comments: 2025-02-10 Aisha Patel: Initial ticket created after cross-functional kickoff. Goal: give customers a compact, explainable UI to declare region/tier fallbacks without writing JSON by hand.
2025-02-12 Marco Liu: UX spike complete. Attached prototype shows node-based rule stacking; flagged need for clearer failure states when fallback chain is empty.
2025-02-13 Sofia Ruiz (Design): Iteration 2 pushes explicit 'compatibility badge' on variants and introduces an inline 'why this will fail' tooltip — low friction for non-expert admins.
2025-02-14 Nate Johnson (Infra): Simulator can reuse recent sampling module from cost-estimator service. Estimate accuracy ~10% for P95; will log assumptions in preview panel.

2025-02-16 Security Review (Rachel Kim): Confirmed simulator will not ingest PII; ensure preview samples are obfuscated and stored only transiently. Security flag: must add opt-in checkbox for enterprise accounts to enable cross-region cost estimates.
2025-02-17 Marco Liu: Implemented basic linter rules and 'apply suggestion' flow. UX note: avoid auto-applying fixes without explicit user confirmation. Need PM copy for messaging.
2025-02-18 Aisha Patel: Pulled into In Review — requesting PM/design review. Please verify acceptance criteria items and sign off on rollout gating (dry-run required for enterprise).
notes: Trade-offs: providing richer simulation increases surface for confusion; we will start with conservative defaults and progressively reveal advanced knobs.
Potential future work: autosuggest fallback variants based on historical success/failure rates and cost budget constraints.
SLO considerations: when cross-region fallback is selected, Console will surface expected P95 degradation and suggest alternative local variants.
QA: create a set of golden policy examples and matching simulator inputs to validate preview outputs across runtime versions.
